paper_title: Particle Physics Implications of a Recent Test of the Gravitational Inverse-Square Law
notes: Solid curve of Fig. 5 (2ps_fac5.eps, vector EPS from the e-print): 68%-confidence upper limit on the gamma5 coupling of massive pseudoscalars to neutrons from the Eot-Wash ISL torsion-balance data (Kapner et al., Ref. [1]), via two-boson-exchange V(r) ~ (g_P^n)^4 K1(2r/lambda) (Eqs. 19-21). Figure y-axis is (g_P^n)^2/(4*pi*hbar*c); converted with g_an = sqrt(4*pi*y). The gamma5 Yukawa coupling g_P^n is already the dimensionless canonical g_an (no 2m_N factor: paper's coupling is dimensionless, not GeV^-1). Proton coupling set to zero, as in the figure: the flat asymptote 2.50e-8 reproduces Gamma = 2.56e-10*beta3 (Table I, beta3=1.3e-4) divided by [N/mu]^2 only (predicted 2.58e-8). Axis calibration anchored on tick strokes; cross-checked: SN1987a dotted line extracted at 7.99e-8 vs quoted 8e-8, previous-ISL dashed flat level matches beta3=2.8e-3. Mass axis meV -> eV. Curve spans 1e-6 eV (flat, extends to arbitrarily low mass) to 1.12e-2 eV where it exits the top of the frame at (g_P)^2/4pi = 4e-2. The paper also bounds vector B-L Yukawa (Fig. 1) and chameleon/dilaton/power-law forces; the gamma5-pseudoscalar-neutron bound is its axion-relevant headline result.
